caption.text:
Missing them will try to convince you that you made a mistake. That maybe you should go back, that maybe you let go too soon, that maybe it could still work if you just tried one more time. But missing someone is not the same thing as being meant to be with them. It just means what you felt was real. 

It means there was love there, connection, something that mattered enough to leave an imprint on you. And of course you feel it now — in the silence, in the absence, in the spaces they used to fill. But pain has a way of romanticizing what hurt you, making you forget why you had to walk away in the first place. 

You didn’t leave without a reason. You didn’t choose distance without knowing something wasn’t right for you. And that truth doesn’t disappear just because you’re lonely, just because healing feels heavier than staying ever did. You can miss them and still know they are not where you belong. 

So if you’re thinking about going back, read this again. Let yourself feel it, but don’t let it lead you somewhere that already broke you. It’s okay to miss them. It’s okay to wish it had worked. But it’s also okay — and necessary — to keep choosing yourself anyway. 🖤

A page from the book ‘Daring To Take Up Space’ by 
Daniell Koepke 📖
